label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
problem_in_my_words: The author's ideas were movements but slides are stills, so he had to talk over his own pictures; a team of agents gave him a loop where he could see a change and ask again.
why: I like that there is a team and that one chair stays empty, but the cast is only promised, never shown, and the figure is a row of greyed cards. 'Ruv-sgit', 'conductor' and 'motion' mean nothing to me yet. I would turn the page for the empty chair, not for the names.
my_sentence: I want my friend to understand why the bus is always late, so that afterwards she can check the live times herself before leaving the house.

by_section.why: Very relatable. I have felt this in a school presentation. The voice note quote is rough but real, and 'The idea was a movement. The slide was a still.' is clear to someone who has never coded.
by_section.quote: I was the bit in between.

by_section.why: The quoted animation passage is about normal users, agents and gold, which I do not follow. 'Agents come with far more volume' and 'the agent doesn't stop' assume I know what the building is for. I take the point that the room saw it, but I could not see it myself.
by_section.quote: Agents come with far more volume.

by_section.why: 'See it, ask for it differently, see it again' is something I did in my first build, so I recognise it. The player and the times (13:50, 15:07, 18:25) are a little fussy but give it a real day feel.
by_section.quote: See it, ask for it differently, see it again.

by_section.why: A name and a conference year from 2012 feels like a lecture. The honest line that a change came back within the hour, not the next keystroke, rescues it, but I would not miss the section.
by_section.quote: Creators need an immediate connection to what they create.

by_section.why: The key idea lands here, but late. 'The build, the check every change had to pass, the brief, the brake' is a list of jargon with no pictures. The glossary gives agent and player but not build, brief, brake or wake. Nine agents sounds big for someone who made one app.
by_section.quote: the build, the check every change had to pass, the brief, the brake that could stop them all

by_section.why: Exactly the size of step I can take tonight: one sentence, no tools. It is short, which I liked, though it comes after a lot of record I had to wade through.
by_section.quote: Write down the one idea you want somebody to understand, and what they should be able to do after.

cut: The long quoted passage in Pressing play, or replace it with one plain sentence of what the animation showed. Trim the clock times in The loop to one. Cut or shrink Inventing on principle to two lines. Move the one-line definition of a factory much earlier.
best_line: The idea was a movement. The slide was a still. I was the bit in between.
worst_moment: Pressing play, the quoted passage: 'Normal users come in and do things... Agents come with far more volume.' It is about users and agents and gold, and as a newcomer I felt it was for programmers.
notes: I do get the factory by the end, as a small team of helpers around one goal that you run for a day, but only because of 'It sounds grander than it is'. Would I start tomorrow? Yes, with the sentence; no, with the factory. Words that lost me: build, brief, brake, wake, ruv-sgit, conductor. Please say in plain words what a brief is, since the sentence I write is called one. Record lines and bands were skipped as instructed.
